valuation_philosophy.model_type: NTA / asset-realisation (wind-down) model, NOT a growth FCF-to-firm DCF
valuation_philosophy.summary: Asset Plus is a single-asset, externally managed, debt-free NZX property vehicle in an explicit, board-reaffirmed lease-up-then-sell-then-wind-up trajectory. Its only property is 6-8 Munroe Lane, Albany (carrying value $105.5m, 75.6% occupied, WALT 9.4 years at Mar-2026). 35 Graham Street was sold and settled 29-Nov-2024, so every historical revenue/earnings CAGR in the Metrics CSV describes a portfolio that no longer exists and must not be extrapolated. Reported NetIncome is dominated by IAS 40 unrealised fair-value revaluations (three consecutive years of write-downs) and is not a cash-earnings measure; FY2026 AFFO was only $0.169m against $2.90m of dividends paid, i.e. distributions are currently funded from the $6.93m cash balance, not from earnings. A conventional revenue-growth/FCF-margin DCF would therefore either capitalise a fictitious growth trajectory or discount an economically meaningless earnings series. Instead this model discounts the path to eventual realisation: (1) project NTA per share forward over a 3-year expected realisation horizon (lease-up completion, marketing, sale, shareholder-approved wind-up), net of interim dividends and residual overhead/cash burn; (2) apply a scenario-specific EXIT PRICE-TO-NTA multiple at the point of realisation, calibrated to the stock's own persistent trading discount to NTA (historically -7.7% at the tightest, FY2019, to -46.9% at the widest, essentially today); (3) discount interim dividends and the year-3 exit value back to present at a COST OF EQUITY built up from NZ risk-free + equity risk premium + single-asset concentration + micro-cap illiquidity + external-manager/governance + execution-risk premia (18.75%), not WACC, because the vehicle carries zero debt and an enterprise-value/FCF-to-firm construction is inapplicable. Net cash ($6.93m) is NOT added on top of the exit value a second time -- it is already embedded inside reported NTA/share, and adding it again would double-count the same asset. A secondary cross-check capitalises fully-leased normalised net rental income ($7.15m, the company's own disclosed potential) at a NZ suburban-office market cap rate (7.5-8.5%), which brackets $0.248-$0.279/share -- comfortably above the base-case realisation value, supporting that the $105.5m independent valuation of Munroe Lane is not obviously stretched even though the market prices the equity at a steep discount to it.

wacc_rationale.method: cost of equity build-up (debt-free vehicle; no WACC/FCF-to-firm construction)
wacc_rationale.notes: Concentration premium reflects 100% single-building/single-submarket exposure (Munroe Lane, Albany). Illiquidity premium reflects a ~NZ$60m market cap and thin NZX turnover. Governance premium reflects Centuria's dual role as external manager and 19.99% shareholder (held just under the 20% Takeovers Code threshold), and the Oct-2025 loss of independent-director status for a Centuria-linked board nominee. Execution premium reflects the open-ended timeline on completing lease-up (75.6% occupied, MILK Orthodontics not yet commenced) in a softening Albany office market (11.7% vacancy Dec-2025, up from 9.5% Jun-2025) before a sale and wind-up can even be put to shareholders. Bull scenario uses a lower cost of equity (15.25%) reflecting reduced execution/governance/illiquidity risk if lease-up and sale proceed smoothly; bear uses a higher cost of equity (22.25%) reflecting a stress path.

inputs.sbc_source: verified nil -- externally managed vehicle with no equity incentive scheme
inputs.interest_income_treatment: not separately stripped -- vehicle's cash is embedded inside reported NTA/share and is not added a second time to an FCF-based enterprise value; there is no FCF-to-firm construction here to double count against

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: not applicable -- wind-down vehicle, no forward growth rate used
historical_growth.notes: All revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are explicitly NOT calculated because the Nov-2024 sale of 35 Graham Street means historical revenue and earnings describe a two-asset portfolio that no longer exists; a trailing CAGR built on that history would not describe the single-asset, wind-down entity APL.NZ is today. Equity (NTA) CAGR is reported for completeness/transparency only -- it captures cap-rate driven fair-value erosion (NTA per share fell from $0.7252 FY2015 to $0.3069 FY2026) and is NOT used as a forward growth driver; the realisation model instead projects NTA per share directly via the scenario NTA paths in `assumptions`.

base.narrative: MILK Orthodontics lease commences and Munroe Lane substantially fully leases over FY2027-28; Albany vacancy stays elevated but stabilises rather than worsening; final leasing incentives complete the modest NTA erosion already visible in FY2026-27, then NTA stabilises. Sale and wind-up executed around FY2029 at a 25% discount to book -- a real private-market/liquidation transaction typically clears tighter than the public market's own trading discount, but transaction costs, agency (external manager) friction, and a soft office investment market still apply.

bull.narrative: Lease-up completes faster and more fully than guided (Aderant + MILK both online, plus incremental tenant demand), Albany vacancy stabilises/improves given the asset's 5-Star Green Star/NABERSNZ credentials versus older secondary stock, cap rates hold or firm slightly, and Munroe Lane sells close to full independent valuation reflecting a well-let, sustainably-designed asset in a recovering North Shore market.

bear.narrative: MILK Orthodontics lease is delayed or falls over, Albany office vacancy keeps rising past 11.7%, further capitalisation-rate softening drives a fourth consecutive year of unrealised write-downs, cash burn from leasing incentives accelerates, the dividend is cut, and the eventual sale is executed at a distressed discount consistent with the market's own current ~-47% trading discount -- i.e. the market is already pricing something close to this outcome.

assumptions.terminal_growth_note: Terminal/perpetuity growth is not used or meaningful for a wind-down vehicle with a finite realisation horizon; the analogous lever here is the EXIT PRICE-TO-NTA MULTIPLE applied at the point of sale/wind-up, calibrated to the stock's own historical P/NTA trading range (-7.7% tightest to -46.9% widest discount).

secondary_affo_cap_rate_check.method: capitalise fully-leased normalised net rental income at a NZ suburban-office market cap rate, net of two years' residual corporate overhead, plus cash, versus zero debt
secondary_affo_cap_rate_check.note: This cross-check brackets $0.248-$0.279/share, comfortably above the base-case realisation value of $0.153/share -- consistent with the base case pricing in real transaction/execution friction on top of a fully-let valuation, and supporting that the $105.5m independent Bayleys valuation of Munroe Lane is not obviously stretched relative to its own disclosed fully-leased income potential.

pnta_history.note: Current price ($0.165) against current NTA ($0.3069) sits at essentially the widest discount this stock has ever traded at, matching almost exactly the FY2026 low. The base-case scenario's implied realisation discount to CURRENT NTA is -50.1% ($0.1533/$0.3069 - 1), i.e. slightly wider even than today's already-extreme market discount, reflecting the additional cash burn, dividend drag and transaction costs baked into the 3-year realisation path. The bull case (-27.7% implied discount to current NTA) sits inside the historical range; the bear case (-72.5%) sits beyond even the historical worst, appropriate for a genuine stress scenario.

entry_price.method: PV of base-case interim dividends plus PV of base-case year-3 exit realisation value, both discounted at the 15% hurdle (NTA already embeds cash, so no separate net-debt adjustment is applied)
entry_price.note: Entry price ($0.168) sits marginally ABOVE the current price ($0.165), meaning buying today already clears roughly a 15% IRR to the base-case realisation path -- consistent with the stock trading at its widest-ever discount to NTA. This is the expected result when the market discount already prices in most of the realistic wind-down friction; it is not a signal that the equity is deeply mispriced in either direction, only that a 15% return is achievable on the base case from here.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity is run over the cost of equity (discount rate) and the realisation/exit price-to-NTA multiple, in place of WACC x terminal growth -- terminal (perpetuity) growth is not a meaningful lever for a finite wind-down vehicle.

sanity_check.description: P/E and EV/EBITDA are structurally meaningless for APL.NZ and are deliberately NOT used as sanity anchors: FY2026 NetIncome is a loss (-$3.164m, EPS -$0.0087) dominated by IAS 40 unrealised fair-value write-downs, so P/E is undefined/negative; there is no clean EBITDA disclosure for an IAS 40 fair-value entity (reported OperatingIncome mixes rental operations with fair-value movements, not a genuine EBITDA line). The governing multiple for this vehicle is PRICE-TO-NTA, and every scenario is checked against APL.NZ's own historical P/NTA trading range (-7.7% tightest, FY2019, to -46.9% widest, essentially today) rather than against generic peer earnings multiples.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base-case intrinsic value ($0.1533) implies a P/NTA of 0.499x against current NTA, i.e. a -50.1% discount that is slightly WIDER than even today's already-extreme -46.2% market discount -- appropriately conservative, not an overshoot, because it additionally discounts three years of cash burn, dividend drag and transaction/wind-up costs that the current spot price does not have to look through on a fixed timeline. Bull case (0.722x NTA, -27.8% implied discount) sits comfortably inside the stock's own 10-year trading range and would require lease-up and sale execution to go better than currently guided. Bear case (0.275x NTA, -72.5% implied discount) sits beyond the historical worst observed discount, appropriate as a genuine stress case (further write-downs + distressed liquidation sale), not a base expectation. Because this is a wind-down vehicle rather than a growth compounder, the standard 'implied upside > 100%' or 'peak-multiple extrapolation' trip conditions used elsewhere in this project do not apply -- the check here is instead whether each scenario's implied P/NTA is a plausible point within (bull, base) or beyond in a clearly labelled stress direction (bear) of the stock's own 10-year empirical P/NTA range, which it is.

warnings: This is an asset-realisation / wind-down valuation, not a growth DCF. There is no assumed perpetual cash-flow-generating business at the end of the horizon -- value is realised via a single-asset sale and shareholder-approved wind-up, with no fixed date disclosed by management as of Aug-2026.
Historical revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are NOT calculated or used because the Nov-2024 sale of 35 Graham Street means all pre-FY2025 trading history describes a larger, now-nonexistent portfolio.

FY2026 AFFO ($0.169m) was far below dividends paid ($2.90m); distributions are currently funded from the cash balance, not earnings, and are explicitly 'subject to quarterly review' with no guaranteed forward payout.

Centuria is both the external manager and a 19.99% shareholder (just under the 20% Takeovers Code threshold), and a Centuria-linked director lost independent status in Oct-2025 -- a real governance/related-party risk to fee levels and the timing/terms of any eventual sale, captured via the governance premium in the cost-of-equity build but not otherwise quantifiable.

No sale process, wind-up resolution, or takeover approach had been announced as of the 6-Aug-2026 AGM; the 3-year realisation horizon used here is this model's own estimate, not a management-disclosed timetable, and is a material source of uncertainty in either direction.
